Assigned boundary review: The trace Casimir, labelled flips and normalized y operators are explicitly defined from matrix units; their recursion and naturality are identities, not a criterion characterizing tensor functors. The source dictionary rewrites the given gl_N Casimir as its sl_N component plus the central correction. It does not recover a Lie-module tensor construction from arbitrary commuting operators. For d=1 there is only x_1=Omega_01 and no adjacent flip; the recursion has no index. Owning batch contract corrected; item carrier unchanged.

Assigned boundary review: The numbered box diagram specifies e, the grading, the parabolic and the character. The centralizer basis and good-grading properties are consequences of this data, not an equivalence classifying arbitrary gradings. The good-grading conditions do not assert that every grading or trace character arises from the displayed left-justified diagram; this item constructs one prescribed pyramid convention. Column numbering fixes the finite box basis; e, the centralizer sums and the trace character are formulas on that basis. No Jordan basis for an arbitrary vector space is selected by this construction. At N=1 the only box lies in column one, e=0, m=0 and g^e=gl_1 in degree zero. Proof 1.1 and 4.1 also allow zero-length rows, which contribute no boxes or centralizer modes. The lower endpoint N=0 is explicitly admitted: the row list may be empty, all box and centralizer index sets are empty, and g, p, h, m and chi are zero (Proof 1.1 and 4.1). At e=0 all matrix units have degree zero, so the good-grading maps retain their stated ranges (2.3). Owning batch contract corrected; item carrier unchanged.

Assigned boundary review: The reduction is defined by a commutator condition in U(p), and its right bimodule action is checked by ideal normalization. This does not state an equivalence between arbitrary associative algebras and Whittaker categories. Whittaker-vector detection is the implication Wh(M)=0 implies M=0 for objects already in the given category; no converse characterization of the category or of finite W-algebras is asserted. Proof 1.1 explicitly gives the scalar-translation automorphism eta; 2.1 through 4.1 check normalizer and module formulas using the given ideals. The detection assertion uses only the choice-free part (3) of the good-grading supplier, rather than its AC-dependent arbitrary-module equivalence. On a one-box pyramid e=m=0, the reduction condition is vacuous, W=U(gl_1), Q=U(gl_1), and every vector is Whittaker. The right action remains multiplication through the prescribed eta automorphism, so the module formulas still hold. For the empty pyramid g=p=m=0, U(g)=C, I_chi=0 and W=Q=C. The category is vector spaces and Wh(M)=M; the subalgebra and bimodule calculations of Proof 2.1 through 4.1 specialize without an absent matrix index. Owning batch contract corrected; item carrier unchanged.

lem-nilpotent-orbit-equivariant-tensor-c.iff-forward: The lemma extends a fixed centralizer-invariant endomorphism and expresses an equivariant polynomial map by trace coefficients and place permutations. These are existence and spanning conclusions, not a biconditional for polynomial maps.
lem-nilpotent-orbit-equivariant-tensor-c.iff-reverse: The displayed expression for covariants is a spanning formula, not a uniqueness claim or a converse recovering the invariant endomorphism from its coefficients. No separate reverse implication is stated.
lem-nilpotent-orbit-equivariant-tensor-c.nonempty-choice: The Statement assumes AC and deps declares it. F1 imports orbit-closure normality with AC; F3 imports complete reducibility and Schur-Weyl invariant lifting. Polynomial polarization is finite, so this row records inherited assumptions rather than asserting an additional arbitrary-index selection.

thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type.iff-forward: The two mutual commutant equalities are both asserted for the prescribed tensor action and every nilpotent Jordan type. The sufficient maximum-string condition for faithfulness is separate; neither part is posed as a biconditional.
thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type.iff-reverse: Injectivity is asserted when there are at least d maximal Jordan strings, without claiming this condition is necessary. The mutual commutant formulas do not constitute a converse characterization of arbitrary nilpotent tensor actions.
thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type.nonempty-choice: AC is a Statement premise and a declared dependency. The full commutant direction consumes the two AC-assuming orbit-normality and covariant-extension suppliers in F3; finite polarization in F2 does not remove those inherited assumptions.

def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra.iff-forward: The cyclotomic algebra is a two-sided quotient by the specified root polynomial, with a PBW dimension and trace. It is not a biconditional identifying every algebra of that dimension with a cyclotomic quotient.
def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra.iff-reverse: The integral-root weight notation and coset chains describe the chosen parameter multiset; the basis and trace properties do not claim to recover its roots uniquely or characterize all Hecke quotients.

endpoints.text: The lower tensor-rank endpoint is defined separately as H_0(a)=C, avoiding x_1. The lower allowed level is l=1, where the Definition gives x_j=a_1 plus the earlier transposition sum; level zero is excluded and repeated roots remain allowed.

def-highest-weight-element-and-connected.iff-reverse: Highest weight crystal is stipulated by a highest vertex and equality with its lowering-generated set. The Definition explicitly denies that connectedness and a highest vertex alone characterize B(lambda); uniqueness for the module crystals is deferred to a separate theorem.

lem-hecke-trace-bilinear-form-and-its-va.iff-forward: The six conclusions define and compute the integral Hecke trace form, its orthonormal standard basis and its KL-basis values. They are pairing identities, not a biconditional criterion for Hecke elements.
lem-hecke-trace-bilinear-form-and-its-va.iff-reverse: Off-diagonal KL pairings lie in v Z[v] and diagonal pairings in 1+v Z[v]; these congruences are not asserted to characterize the KL basis or to imply bar invariance.

lem-the-lefschetz-operator-factors-throu.iff-forward: The operator decomposition and rescaled form identity hold for the prescribed deleted-word maps; reducedness gives positivity of the factors. The ascent-detection biconditional in F3 is an imported fact, not the conclusion of this lemma.
lem-the-lefschetz-operator-factors-throu.iff-reverse: Positive deleted-word scaling is concluded for reduced expressions; no converse characterizes reduced words from those scaling signs, nor is the factorization claimed to imply hard Lefschetz.

lem-the-minimal-rouquier-differential-su.iff-forward: Right-module retraction and concentration of reduced cohomology yield an injectivity criterion and its ascent application. These are conditional implications; no equivalence between injectivity and the specified cohomology concentration is claimed.
lem-the-minimal-rouquier-differential-su.iff-reverse: Injectivity in the stated internal degrees does not claim to recover linearity or minimality of a Rouquier complex. Clause (4) expressly requires separate form compatibility and operator commutation.

def-regular-integral-category-o-block-an.nonempty-choice: The Definition explicitly carries AC from linkage-block and standard/costandard theory and declares def-axiom-of-choice. Its finite dot orbit labels and the projective covers use that supplied theory; choosing the antidominant representative via w_0 adds no arbitrary-index selection.

def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-int.iff-forward: Projective functor is a stipulated direct summand of a finite tensor-block functor. Its exactness and closure properties are conclusions about that class, not an equivalence between exact functors and projective functors.
def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-int.iff-reverse: The summand definition does not claim every exact projective-preserving endofunctor has such a tensor presentation. Closure under composition asserts a summand of the ambient tensor functor, expressly allowing returning complementary blocks.
def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-int.endpoints: There is no interval of weights or limiting functor in this construction on the fixed regular block. Tensor dimension zero and the trivial one-dimensional tensor module are separately evaluated as the zero and identity functors in Basic properties.

def-the-antidominant-projective-and-the-.iff-forward: The selected projective cover defines the Hom functor and its endomorphism-ring action; injectivity and the once-each Verma flag are properties of that cover, not an equivalence characterizing arbitrary Hom functors.
def-the-antidominant-projective-and-the-.iff-reverse: Changing the antidominant cover by an isomorphism induces a natural equivalence, without claiming that arbitrary equivalent Hom functors identify projective covers or that the functor is an equivalence of module categories.
def-the-antidominant-projective-and-the-.nonempty-choice: Definition, opening assumption and fixed projective: The opening premise inherits AC from the block and enough-projectives suppliers; P is one fixed projective cover. Its uniqueness up to isomorphism makes the Hom functor independent of that single choice, without claiming the supplier theory is choice-free.

def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-.iff-forward: The quotient by positive-degree Weyl invariants defines C, with its doubled grading and finite dimension from the cited freeness theorem. It does not characterize arbitrary graded algebras of dimension |W|.
def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-.iff-reverse: The auxiliary type-A permutation quotient is a concrete presentation of the same coinvariant algebra; that isomorphism does not claim a converse recovering a Weyl group from an arbitrary finite graded quotient.

def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-i.iff-forward: Induction defines M_S and finite tensor summands define the family, with fibers over actual residue fields. These constructions do not characterize all flat highest-weight families or identify every localization fiber with a complex fiber.
def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-i.iff-reverse: The selected central component is specified by its origin block and CRT projectors. No converse claims that the entire tensor family belongs to that block, or that generic parameters must be integral.
def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-i.nonempty-choice: Definition, opening assumption and Selected components: AC is expressly inherited from block theory and declared as a dependency. The finite central-character separation and CRT projectors in Selected components add only finite selections; they do not replace the inherited premise by finite choice.
def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-i.endpoints: The deformation parameter runs through Spec of a localization, not a real interval with limiting endpoints. The origin, generic point and non-complex residue fields are included by the actual specialization definition; no limiting operation identifies these fibers.

def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-couni.iff-forward: Onto-wall and out-of-wall tensor projections define theta_s and its adjunction maps. Their exactness and two standard labels do not assert a biconditional classifying exact endofunctors of the block.
def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-couni.iff-reverse: The equality of standard evaluations is not itself claimed to imply natural equivalence here; independence from the auxiliary weight is explicitly discharged by the later classification theorem in justified_by.
def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-couni.endpoints: The weights lie on a regular dominant chamber and one specified dominant wall with stabilizer {1,s}. This is fixed facet data, not an interval limiting to a multiple-wall point; larger stabilizers are excluded by the stated hypothesis.

iff-forward.text: The word Equivalently in clause (3) restates the finite connected graded algebra conclusion of (2): the one-dimensional top socle and nondegenerate multiplication pairing make C graded Gorenstein. Proof 4.1 identifies the socle and 5.1 proves the pairing.

iff-reverse.text: For this finite connected graded C, the Gorenstein description with one-dimensional socle in degree 2N gives the pairing formulation: a nonzero homogeneous c generates an ideal whose largest nonzero degree is in the socle, hence there is b of complementary degree with cb nonzero, as in Proof 5.1. This restatement does not characterize general invariant rings.

lem-the-harmonic-complement-of-the-coinv.iff-forward: The harmonic subspace exists and gives multiplication and quotient isomorphisms; any W-stable graded complement has these properties. This is a construction of complements, not a biconditional for kernels of arbitrary differential operators.
lem-the-harmonic-complement-of-the-coinv.iff-reverse: The simultaneous invariant differential kernel is one admissible harmonic complement. No converse identifies every graded complement with that specific kernel, and the Statement explicitly excludes using the quadratic Laplacian alone.

lem-the-nilpotent-central-fiber-is-a-red.iff-forward: The fixed basic invariant quotient is a reduced domain with a specified Hilbert series, and every central reduction has that PBW associated graded. These are consequences of invariant theory, not a biconditional for arbitrary central quotients.
lem-the-nilpotent-central-fiber-is-a-red.iff-reverse: The shared nilpotent associated graded is not claimed to determine the central character or the filtered central reduction up to isomorphism; the Statement gives the identification separately for every character.

thm-duflo-joseph-g-finite-endomorphisms-.iff-forward: The specified enveloping action induces an algebra isomorphism onto the g-finite endomorphisms of a Verma module, with the annihilator and multiplicity formulas. No biconditional characterizes arbitrary highest-weight modules.
thm-duflo-joseph-g-finite-endomorphisms-.iff-reverse: The zero-weight Hom dimension formula does not claim to characterize Verma modules among all modules. The inverse algebra map belongs to the asserted isomorphism, not a separate converse hypothesis.
thm-duflo-joseph-g-finite-endomorphisms-.nonempty-choice: AC is stated and declared in deps. F2 and F4 import finite-length category-O and duality theory; F6 imports the AC-assuming nilpotent central-fiber and harmonic multiplicity suppliers. Proof 5.1 records this inheritance, not a new arbitrary-index basis selection.

prop-base-change-freeness-and-specializa.iff-forward: The four assertions are endomorphism identification, freeness, base change, local freeness and an origin-fiber isomorphism test for the specified deformed family. They give sufficient hypotheses, not a classification of all deformation families.
prop-base-change-freeness-and-specializa.iff-reverse: The origin-fiber test is restricted to maps in D_R(lambda); no reverse criterion claims that an arbitrary morphism with an invertible fiber belongs to that family or that locally free Hom modules are globally free for arbitrary summands.

lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-gr.iff-forward: The standard-class map is a group isomorphism and transports theta_s to right multiplication by 1+s. Its word-product formula concerns the specified composition order, not a biconditional determining functors from their classes.
lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-gr.iff-reverse: Equality of operators on the Grothendieck group is not asserted to imply natural isomorphism of functors. The reverse-order clause computes a different composition rather than establishing a converse characterization.
lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-gr.nonempty-choice: The Statement carries AC from the regular-block standard-basis theory in F1 and the wall-crossing two-factor flag in F2. Expanding a finite reduced word into subexpressions uses only finite sums and adds no stronger selection principle.

lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standa.iff-forward: The two-factor Verma flag and exactness give the stated sum of standard classes and flag multiplicities. These are implications for the specified wall crossing, not an equivalence classifying two-step extensions.
lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standa.iff-reverse: A sum of two standard classes does not imply a split object or identify an extension. The Statement expressly retains possibly nonsplit flags and does not assert a converse to the multiplicity formula.

lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-t.iff-forward: The prescribed reduced-word composition has the top projective once and only lower other summands by the triangular BGG matrix. This is a decomposition theorem, not a biconditional identifying words from their top projective.
lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-t.iff-reverse: Every indecomposable projective is obtained as a summand of some word, without asserting that any chosen summand determines a unique reduced word or that two word compositions with the same top label are isomorphic.
lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-t.nonempty-choice: Statement and Facts F1/F3: AC is an explicit premise and dependency inherited through F1 projective covers, finite-length decompositions and Verma flags, and F3 BGG reciprocity and linkage. The subsequent finite triangular multiplicity calculation does not remove those supplier assumptions.
